abstract: Plant viruses are a diverse class of infectious agents affecting agricultural crop production, plant health, and international movement of plant material. While availability and accessibility of scientific data related to plant viruses is essential for plant protection activities, scientific research, diagnostics, plant breeding, and beyond, publicly available data on plant viruses are at present not easily accessible; they are non-standardized, scattered across different resources, poorly interlinked, and not easily searchable by scientists or digital agents. We present PVDive (Plant Virus Diversity Database; https://pvdive.dsmz.de), a freely accessible resource providing high-quality, standardized, and integrated data associated with plant viruses. PVDive primarily offers information at the level of individual plant virus isolates and samples originating from the plant virus collection of the Leibniz Institute DSMZ (Germany). The data are integrated with information on plant virus species and host plants available in existing public resources and their access is centralized in a single platform. Through an intuitive, user-friendly interface with a number of search functionalities and a RESTful application programming interface, PVDive improves findability, accessibility, retrievability, and interoperability of plant virus data. To support data exploration, the platform also includes tools such as advanced search, sequence viewer, host gallery, and interactive data views.
